target: /pages/faq — the left-column picture behind three of the five category titles
note: Three new pictures for the FAQ category blocks. The other two blocks (Products & Usage, Ingredients & Safety) are being filled from images that already exist, so only these three are generated. GENERATED AT 4:3 BECAUSE THAT IS WHAT THE BLOCK IS. The injected carries aspect-ratio 4/3 with object-fit cover, so anything squarer or wider loses the surplus axis permanently at every viewport. The two existing images going into the other blocks are 1:1 and will be cropped by the theme; these three are cut to the shape of the hole from the start. THE FIVE BLOCKS MUST READ AS ONE SET. The title sits ON the picture in white, so every frame needs a deep ground and a quiet top third for the type. Graphite #1A1A1A, one large soft key, 85mm-class compression and fine grain are therefore held constant across all three, exactly as the cream-application-faces wave held its framing constant — only the subject changes. LUMA IS EXCLUDED FROM ALL THREE, and for two different reasons worth separating. On the box it is not a judgement call: luma() in generate-multi.py ignores ref_files entirely, so it cannot be shown the brand mark and would invent one — the same failure FLUX.2 is already barred for. On the two face shots it refused this subject family repeatedly on 2026-08-22 and costs three to four minutes per attempt to discover that again. FLUX.2 self-skips the box slot (the script bars it from reference shots) and runs on the two face slots, which carry no branding.

slots.title: Orders & Shipping — packed white box, brand mark on the lid
slots.prompt: Product photograph, landscape format, close on a single white rigid cardboard box sitting closed on a seamless deep graphite surface, colour #1A1A1A, that falls to near-black at the edges of the frame. The box is a plain matte white cube-shaped carton roughly as tall as it is deep and half again as wide, lid down and squarely closed, with one slim band of smooth white paper tape running across the top seam and a little way down the front face. Its corners are crisp, its faces are clean and unmarked, and the surface is uncoated matte board that takes the light softly rather than reflecting it. The box is turned about twenty degrees so the lid and one front face are both visible, filling roughly two thirds of the frame width and sitting low, with clear empty ground above it. Printed on the lid, small and centred, is the mark supplied in the reference image, reproduced exactly: a fine black double-helix strand of short vertical dashes at the left, then the single word "Skingenetix" in a bold italic lowercase sans-serif with a capital S, in black. That mark is the only printed element anywhere in the picture: every other face and every other surface is completely blank. One large soft key from the upper left rakes across the lid and throws a soft contact shadow to the right, with one dim cool fill on the shadow side so the white board keeps texture instead of blowing out. 85mm at f5.6, shallow depth of field with the front top edge sharp, fine film grain, neutral whites, quiet and expensive.

slots.title: Returns & Refunds — she is pleased with what the phone says
slots.prompt: Editorial photograph, landscape format, close on one woman between thirty five and forty five years old, holding her mobile phone up and slightly to one side and reading it. The frame holds her from the top of the head to just below the collarbone, her face a little right of centre, with the phone entering the lower left of the frame in her own hand and held at chest height so the screen is angled away from the camera and completely invisible. She is genuinely pleased by what she is reading: a real unforced smile that reaches the eyes and creases them slightly, lips parted just enough to show a little of the upper teeth, chin tipped a fraction down toward the screen and eyes down on it. Her free hand is relaxed and out of frame. Almost no makeup. Real skin kept real: visible pores, natural fine lines at the eye and around the mouth, natural marks, fine down catching the light along the jaw, and uneven sheen so some areas read matte and others slightly shiny. The texture never resolves into swirls, whorls, concentric rings or any repeating pattern anywhere. Hair simply worn and swept back from the face. She wears a plain dark crew-neck top with no pattern and no visible seams or logos. Behind her a seamless deep graphite backdrop, colour #1A1A1A, falling to near-black at the top of the frame so the upper third is quiet and almost empty. One large soft key from the upper left models the cheekbone and jaw, with one dim cool fill on the shadow side. 85mm at f2.8, shallow depth of field with her eyes sharp and the phone falling gently soft, fine film grain, natural skin tones, quiet and expensive.

slots.title: Skincare & Routine — a drop of clear serum going onto the cheek
slots.prompt: Macro beauty photograph, landscape format, extremely close on the cheek of one woman between thirty five and forty five years old, so close that the cheek and cheekbone fill almost the whole frame and only the corner of one eye and the edge of the nose enter at the left. The skin is the subject. A slim clear glass dropper tube comes in from the upper right and is held vertically just above the cheekbone, its tip about one fingertip-width clear of the skin. That tube is roughly eight times longer than it is wide, about as long as the width of three fingers, plain clear glass with no markings, and only its lower half is in frame. Held at its tip is one single transparent droplet, water-clear and colourless, catching a bright specular highlight, with a second identical droplet already resting on the cheekbone below it as a small clear domed bead that sits on the skin and lets the pores show straight through it. The fingers holding the tube are relaxed with short natural unpainted nails, and only the fingertips and the first knuckle are in frame. Real skin kept real at this magnification: individual pores, fine down catching the light, natural fine lines, one or two small natural marks, and uneven sheen so some areas read matte and others slightly shiny. The texture never resolves into swirls, whorls, concentric rings or any repeating pattern. Behind and beyond her a seamless deep graphite backdrop, colour #1A1A1A, falling to near-black at the top of the frame so the upper third is quiet and almost empty. One large soft key from the upper left rakes low across the cheek so the skin texture reads, with one dim cool fill on the shadow side. 100mm macro at f5.6, the droplet and the skin around it sharp, the dropper tip falling gently soft, fine film grain, natural skin tones, quiet and expensive.
